claim: This study performed the first CRISPR screen to date in human polarized epithelial cells.
source: In this way, we performed the first CRISPR screen to date in human polarized epithelial cells.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this is the first CRISPR screen in human polarized epithelial cells in the abstract.

claim: Knockout of TM9SF4 causes polarization defects in epithelial cells.
source: Using high-resolution microscopy, we detected polarization defects and mislocalization of DPP4 to late endosomes/lysosomes after knockout of TM9SF4, anoctamin 8, and ARHGAP33, confirming the identification of novel factors for epithelial polarization and apical cargo secretion.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that knockout of TM9SF4 results in polarization defects detected by high-resolution microscopy.

claim: Knockout of anoctamin 8 causes polarization defects in epithelial cells.
source: Using high-resolution microscopy, we detected polarization defects and mislocalization of DPP4 to late endosomes/lysosomes after knockout of TM9SF4, anoctamin 8, and ARHGAP33, confirming the identification of novel factors for epithelial polarization and apical cargo secretion.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that knockout of anoctamin 8 results in polarization defects detected by high-resolution microscopy.

claim: Knockout of ARHGAP33 causes polarization defects in epithelial cells.
source: Using high-resolution microscopy, we detected polarization defects and mislocalization of DPP4 to late endosomes/lysosomes after knockout of TM9SF4, anoctamin 8, and ARHGAP33, confirming the identification of novel factors for epithelial polarization and apical cargo secretion.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that knockout of ARHGAP33 results in polarization defects detected by high-resolution microscopy.

claim: DPP4 mislocalizes to late endosomes/lysosomes after knockout of TM9SF4.
source: Using high-resolution microscopy, we detected polarization defects and mislocalization of DPP4 to late endosomes/lysosomes after knockout of TM9SF4, anoctamin 8, and ARHGAP33, confirming the identification of novel factors for epithelial polarization and apical cargo secretion.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states DPP4 mislocalizes to late endosomes/lysosomes after TM9SF4 knockout.

claim: DPP4 mislocalizes to late endosomes/lysosomes after knockout of anoctamin 8.
source: Using high-resolution microscopy, we detected polarization defects and mislocalization of DPP4 to late endosomes/lysosomes after knockout of TM9SF4, anoctamin 8, and ARHGAP33, confirming the identification of novel factors for epithelial polarization and apical cargo secretion.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states DPP4 mislocalizes to late endosomes/lysosomes after anoctamin 8 knockout.

claim: DPP4 mislocalizes to late endosomes/lysosomes after knockout of ARHGAP33.
source: Using high-resolution microscopy, we detected polarization defects and mislocalization of DPP4 to late endosomes/lysosomes after knockout of TM9SF4, anoctamin 8, and ARHGAP33, confirming the identification of novel factors for epithelial polarization and apical cargo secretion.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states DPP4 mislocalizes to late endosomes/lysosomes after ARHGAP33 knockout.

claim: Epithelial cells build specialized apical and basolateral plasma membrane domains during polarization.
source: During polarization, epithelial cells assume their characteristic shape by building specialized apical- and basolateral plasma membrane (PM) domains (Rodriguez-Boulan and Macara, 2014; Apodaca et al., 2012), which are separated by junctional complexes and characterized by a specific composition of lipids and proteins (Martin-Belmonte et al., 2007).
evidence: The introduction explicitly states this with supporting citations.

claim: Apical and basolateral plasma membrane domains are separated by junctional complexes.
source: During polarization, epithelial cells assume their characteristic shape by building specialized apical- and basolateral plasma membrane (PM) domains (Rodriguez-Boulan and Macara, 2014; Apodaca et al., 2012), which are separated by junctional complexes and characterized by a specific composition of lipids and proteins (Martin-Belmonte et al., 2007).
evidence: The introduction explicitly states this with supporting citations.

claim: Apical and basolateral plasma membrane domains are characterized by a specific composition of lipids and proteins.
source: During polarization, epithelial cells assume their characteristic shape by building specialized apical- and basolateral plasma membrane (PM) domains (Rodriguez-Boulan and Macara, 2014; Apodaca et al., 2012), which are separated by junctional complexes and characterized by a specific composition of lipids and proteins (Martin-Belmonte et al., 2007).
evidence: The introduction explicitly states this with supporting citations.

claim: Microvillus inclusion disease (MVID) is an autosomal-recessive enteropathy.
source: Microvillus inclusion disease (MVID) is an autosomal-recessive enteropathy (Cutz et al., 1989), characterized by intractable diarrhea in neonates (Cutz et al., 1989; Ruemmele et al., 2006).
evidence: The introduction explicitly states this with supporting citations.

claim: MVID is characterized by intractable diarrhea in neonates.
source: Microvillus inclusion disease (MVID) is an autosomal-recessive enteropathy (Cutz et al., 1989), characterized by intractable diarrhea in neonates (Cutz et al., 1989; Ruemmele et al., 2006).
evidence: The introduction explicitly states this with supporting citations.

claim: Mutations in MYO5B are causative for MVID.
source: Our studies identified mutations in MYO5B, STX3, and STXBP2 to be causative for MVID (Müller et al., 2008; Ruemmele et al., 2010; Wiegerinck et al., 2014; Vogel et al., 2017b)
evidence: The introduction explicitly states this with supporting citations to the authors' previous work.

claim: Mutations in STX3 are causative for MVID.
source: Our studies identified mutations in MYO5B, STX3, and STXBP2 to be causative for MVID (Müller et al., 2008; Ruemmele et al., 2010; Wiegerinck et al., 2014; Vogel et al., 2017b)
evidence: The introduction explicitly states this with supporting citations to the authors' previous work.

claim: Mutations in STXBP2 are causative for MVID.
source: Our studies identified mutations in MYO5B, STX3, and STXBP2 to be causative for MVID (Müller et al., 2008; Ruemmele et al., 2010; Wiegerinck et al., 2014; Vogel et al., 2017b)
evidence: The introduction explicitly states this with supporting citations to the authors' previous work.

claim: DPP4 is a type II transmembrane protein.
source: The brush-border hydrolase DPP4 is a type II transmembrane protein.
evidence: The introduction explicitly states this fact about DPP4.

claim: DPP4 is heavily modified with N- and O-linked glycans in its extracellular domain.
source: It is heavily modified with N- and O-linked glycans in its extracellular domain (Misumi et al., 1992; Baricault et al., 1995; Fan et al., 1997), which have been suggested to be critical apical sorting determinants of DPP4 (Alfalah et al., 2002).
evidence: The introduction explicitly states this with supporting citations.

claim: N- and O-linked glycans have been suggested to be critical apical sorting determinants of DPP4.
source: It is heavily modified with N- and O-linked glycans in its extracellular domain (Misumi et al., 1992; Baricault et al., 1995; Fan et al., 1997), which have been suggested to be critical apical sorting determinants of DPP4 (Alfalah et al., 2002).
evidence: The introduction explicitly states this with supporting citation.

claim: Surface DPP4 signal is significantly increased during 18-21 days of CaCo2 cell polarization.
source: Here, we used a period of 18–21 days, during which surface DPP4 signal is significantly increased in the course of cell surface expansion and specialized polarized trafficking processes (Figure 1B).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this and references Figure 1B showing the data.

claim: 89 gRNAs were significantly enriched in the sorted cell population from the CRISPR screen.
source: Subsequent analysis using GenePattern and Galaxy analysis tools enabled the identification of 89 gRNAs significantly enriched in the sorted cell population (p<0.05) and represented genes whose downregulation had resulted in reduced DPP4 surface release (Figure 1D and E, Supplementary file 1A and B).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this with p-value and references to figures and supplementary files.

claim: Colchicine treatment does not cause a reduction in surface DPP4 signal in CaCo2 cells.
source: This treatment would induce VAC formation, but we found no change in apical DPP4 signaling (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B) and therefore concluded that VAC formation should not interfere with the FACS-based screening approach.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this with reference to supplementary figures.

claim: All seven selected KO cell lines show varying extents of DPP4 surface reduction.
source: All KO cell lines show varying extents of DPP4 surface reduction, with PIP5K1C-KO displaying the strongest and ANO8-KO the mildest effect.
evidence: Figure 3C caption explicitly states this finding.

claim: PIP5K1C knockout causes approximately 75% reduction in DPP4 surface localization.
source: The strongest effect on DPP4 surface localization was caused by interference with PIP5K1C (~75% reduction), followed by TM9SF4, TMEM110, and GALNT2 (~50% reduction).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this quantification.

claim: TM9SF4, TMEM110, and GALNT2 knockouts cause approximately 50% reduction in DPP4 surface localization.
source: The strongest effect on DPP4 surface localization was caused by interference with PIP5K1C (~75% reduction), followed by TM9SF4, TMEM110, and GALNT2 (~50% reduction).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this quantification.

claim: ANO8, MTMR2, and ARHGAP33 knockouts cause approximately 30% reduction in DPP4 surface localization.
source: Interestingly, ANO8-, MTMR2-, and ARHGAP33-KOs showed the mildest phenotype (~30% reduction) (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this quantification with reference to figures.

claim: All KO cell lines have severe defects in forming a single, central lumen in 3D cyst assays.
source: We found that all KO cell lines had severe defects in forming a single, central lumen, but rather established multiple or no lumina (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding with reference to figures.

claim: TM9SF4, MTMR2, and ANO8 KO cell lines display aberrant intracellular accumulation of DPP4 in 3D cysts.
source: Although DPP4 was localized in the apical PM domains in all KO cell lines, TM9SF4-, MTMR2-, and ANO8-KO cell lines additionally displayed aberrant intracellular accumulation of DPP4 (Figure 4A and C).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding with reference to figures.

claim: All KO cell lines have conspicuous clusters of ectopic microvilli.
source: In contrast to CaCo2 WT cells, all KO cell lines had conspicuous clusters of ectopic microvilli (Figure 5A–E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding with reference to figures.

claim: Most KO lines show late endosomal/lysosomal endomembrane system characterized by partly giant, spherical organelles.
source: However, in most KO lines, the late endosomal/lysosomal endomembrane system was characterized – if not even dominated− by partly giant, spherical organelles (in addition to normal MVBs) − at the expense of normal lysosomes (Figure 5B and E, Figure 6C–G, double arrowheads).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding with reference to figures.

claim: In TM9SF4 and ANO8 KO cells, enlarged endolysosomes reach dimensions of up to 2 × 6 µm in diameter.
source: Especially in TM9SF4- and ANO8-KO, they reached dimensions of up to 2 × 6 µm in diameter (e.g., Figure 6C), in other KO cell lines only diameters of approximately 500 nm.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this quantification with reference to figures.

claim: All KO cell lines show patchy distribution or complete absence of apical microvilli.
source: Regarding the general architecture of the brush-border, SEM and actin fluorescence microscopy revealed more or less severe irregularities in in all KO cell lines studied here (Figures 7—9). They included patchy distribution or complete absence of apical microvilli, together with the occurrence of extremely long microvilli (Figure 7B–H).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding with reference to figures.

claim: DPP4 mislocalizes to subapical compartments in ARHGAP33, TM9SF4, and ANO8 KO cell lines.
source: While DPP4 was mislocalized to subapical compartments in ARHGAP33-, TM9SF4-, and ANO8-KO cell lines, PIP5K1C- and MTMR2-KOs displayed DPP4 localization to large, actin-rich, basolateral structures, reminiscent of microvillus inclusions, observed by EM.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding.

claim: PIP5K1C and MTMR2 KO cells display DPP4 localization to large, actin-rich, basolateral structures reminiscent of microvillus inclusions.
source: While DPP4 was mislocalized to subapical compartments in ARHGAP33-, TM9SF4-, and ANO8-KO cell lines, PIP5K1C- and MTMR2-KOs displayed DPP4 localization to large, actin-rich, basolateral structures, reminiscent of microvillus inclusions, observed by EM.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding.

claim: APN delocalizes to actin-rich intracellular compartments only in ARHGAP33 KO cells.
source: Interestingly, we found APN delocalized to actin-rich intracellular compartments only in ARHGAP33-KO cells (Figure 8—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding with reference to supplementary figure.

claim: The apical localization of SI remains unaltered upon deletion of the selected genes.
source: However, the apical localization of SI remained unaltered upon deletion of the selected genes (Figure 8—figure supplement 2A–H).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding with reference to supplementary figure.

claim: TEER of ARHGAP33 KO cells increases substantially around day 7 of measurement.
source: Transepithelial electric resistance (TEER) measurements of filter-grown, polarized 2D monolayers of WT and KO cell lines revealed an increase of TEER after measurement day 7 upon KO of ARHGAP33, while TEER of the other KO cell lines remained comparable to those of WT cells (Figure 10I).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding with reference to figure.

claim: Enlarged, poorly structured organelles in TM9SF4, ANO8, and ARHGAP33 KO cells show distinct Lamp1, Lamp3, or CathepsinD immunogold label.
source: Membrane or contents of those compartments showed distinct Lamp1, Lamp3, or CathepsinD immunogold label, respectively, in all three KO cell lines (Figure 11A, C and D).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding with reference to figures.

claim: Enlarged organelles in TM9SF4, ANO8, and ARHGAP33 KO cells are acidic as shown by DAMP labeling.
source: Successful immunogold detection of the previously internalized acidotropic reagent DAMP provided further evidence for the clearly acidic nature of those organelles, justifying their classification as types of modified endolysosomes/(autophago)lysosomes (Figure 11B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1F and G).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding with reference to figures.

claim: Enlarged organelles in TM9SF4, ANO8, and ARHGAP33 KO cells regularly contain mislocalized DPP4.
source: They regularly contained mislocalized DPP4 (Figure 11C and D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1F and G).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding with reference to figures.

claim: After serum deprivation overnight, giant, poorly structured compartments in TM9SF4, ANO8, and ARHGAP33 KO cells disappear and reformed lysosomes of normal size and morphology are observed.
source: After serum deprivation overnight almost all the giant, poorly structured, faint compartments had disappeared, likely due to autophagic removal, and reformed lysosomes of normal size and morphology were regularly observed (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H–K).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding with reference to supplementary figures.

claim: Imbalances in cellular PIP-pools might be the basis for the observed phenotypes in PIP5K1C and MTMR2 KO cells.
source: PIP5K1C and MTMR2 are involved in the regulation of PIP pools accounting for apical PM composition. Therefore, imbalances in cellular PIP-pools might be the basis for the observed phenotypes.
evidence: The discussion section explicitly proposes this mechanism.

claim: MTMR2 and PIP5K1C mRNAs are expressed predominantly in polarized 2D cultures and downregulated in 3D cysts of MDCK cells.
source: Interestingly, the mRNAs of MTMR2 and PIP5K1C mRNAs were shown to be expressed predominantly in polarized 2D cultures, whereas they were downregulated in 3D cysts of MDCK cells, indicating differential PIP regulation in 2D polarized monolayers and polarization 'de novo' (Román-Fernández et al., 2018).
evidence: The discussion section explicitly states this with supporting citation.

claim: ANO8 and TMEM110 might regulate polarization via the control of Ca2+ influx and signaling.
source: The ER-PM contact site proteins ANO8 and TMEM110 might regulate polarization via the control of Ca2+ influx and signaling (Jha et al., 2019; Quintana et al., 2015)
evidence: The discussion section explicitly proposes this mechanism with supporting citations.

claim: TM9SF4 possibly controls polarization through generation of lipid microdomains and pH regulation.
source: while TM9SF4, which has been implicated in the regulation of glycolipids in the Golgi apparatus (Perrin et al., 2015) and VH-ATPase assembly (Lozupone et al., 2015), possibly controls polarization through generation of lipid microdomains and pH regulation.
evidence: The discussion section explicitly proposes this mechanism with supporting citations.

claim: GALNT2 might contribute to establishing polarity via its role as O-glycosylating enzyme in the Golgi apparatus.
source: GALNT2 might contribute to establishing polarity via its role as O-glycosylating enzyme in the Golgi apparatus
evidence: The discussion section explicitly proposes this mechanism.

claim: ARHGAP33 as a GAP-protein for Cdc42 might be critically involved in polarization and polarized traffic.
source: and ARHGAP33 as a GAP-protein for the small GTPase Cdc42 might itself be critically involved in polarization and polarized traffic as well (Nakazawa et al., 2016).
evidence: The discussion section explicitly proposes this mechanism with supporting citation.

claim: Ca2+ levels in the Golgi apparatus regulate apical sorting of GPI-anchored proteins in polarized epithelial cells.
source: Ca2+ levels in the Golgi apparatus, for example, were shown to regulate apical sorting of GPI-anchored proteins in polarized epithelial cells (Lebreton et al., 2021).
evidence: The discussion section explicitly states this with supporting citation.

claim: Mislocalization of DPP4 in ANO8 KOs to endosomal/lysosomal compartments could result from aberrant, Ca2+-dependent sorting in the Golgi apparatus.
source: Thus, mislocalization of DPP4 in ANO8-KOs to endosomal/lysosomal compartments could result from aberrant, Ca2+-dependent sorting in the Golgi apparatus.
evidence: The discussion section explicitly proposes this mechanism.

claim: Lipid microdomains and pH regulation represent major sorting determinants of apical cargo in the Golgi.
source: Finally, lipid microdomains and pH regulation represent major sorting determinants of apical cargo in the Golgi (Hallermann, 2014; Medina et al., 2015; de Araujo et al., 2017; Schuck and Simons, 2004).
evidence: The discussion section explicitly states this with supporting citations.

claim: Mistargeting of apical cargo into lysosomal compartments may coincide with defects in glycosphingolipid synthesis and/or V-ATPase-mediated pH regulation caused by TM9SF4 KO.
source: Therefore, it is plausible to assume that the observed mistargeting of apical cargo into lysosomal compartments may coincide with defects in glycosphingolipid synthesis and/or V-ATPase-mediated pH regulation, caused by TM9SF4-KO (Lozupone et al., 2015; Levic et al., 2020; Levic and Bagnat, 2021).
evidence: The discussion section explicitly proposes this mechanism with supporting citations.

claim: UNC45A has been associated with syndromal diarrhea and cholestasis.
source: Apart from the association of Unc-45 Myosin Chaperone A (UNC45A) with syndromal diarrhea and cholestasis, no other genes identified in our CRISPR screen have been published in this context to date (Esteve et al., 2018; Li et al., 2022; Dulcaux-Loras et al., 2022).
evidence: The discussion section explicitly states this with supporting citations.

claim: MVID caused by mutations of myo5b, stx3, stxbp2, or unc45a is characterized by pathological accumulation of considerably enlarged autophagosomal and/or lysosomal organelles in the cell periphery.
source: However, MVID caused by mutations of myo5b, stx3, stxbp2, or unc45a is a prominent example for pathological accumulation of considerably enlarged autophagosomal and/or lysosomal organelles in the cell periphery.
evidence: The discussion section explicitly states this.

claim: In mucolipidosis type IV, the absence of mucolipin-1 and -3 induced aberrant swelling of late endosomal/lysosomal organelles in enterocytes of newly born mice.
source: Moreover, abnormal late endosomes/lysosomes with close resemblance to the respective faint, poorly structured lysosomal compartments in the phenotypes we describe here were implicated in another neonatal intestinal disorder, namely, human mucolipidosis type IV. In newly born mice, the absence of mucolipin-1 and -3 induced aberrant swelling of those organelles in enterocytes, diminished apical endocytosis from the intestinal lumen, caused diarrhea, and delayed growth (Remis et al., 2014).
evidence: The discussion section explicitly states this with supporting citation.

claim: Several genes identified in the CRISPR screen have been associated with neuropathies or myopathies.
source: Finally, it should be noted that several genes identified in our screening have been associated with neuropathies or myopathies (Charcot–Marie–Tooth syndrome [MTMR2]; Dyggve–Melchior–Clausen syndrome [DYM]) (Denais et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2019).
evidence: The discussion section explicitly states this with supporting citations.

claim: CaCo2 cells were transduced with the human lentiviral GeCKOv2 CRISPR-library at a low multiplicity of infection (0.2).
source: First, we generated Cas9-expressing CaCo2 cells and then transduced two biological replicates at a low multiplicity of infection (MOI) (0.2) using the human lentiviral GeCKOv2 CRISPR-library, selecting for successful viral integration with antibiotic treatment with puromycin.
evidence: The results section explicitly describes this experimental procedure.

claim: Polarized CaCo2 cells were cultured for 18 days before FACS sorting in the CRISPR screen.
source: We then seeded the infected CaCo2 cultures at high density and allowed the confluent monolayers to further polarize and differentiate for 18 days.
evidence: The results section explicitly describes this experimental procedure.

claim: Approximately 10% of cells with lowest surface DPP4 signal were sorted by FACS in the CRISPR screen.
source: Next, polarized cells were detached, stained for endogenous DPP4, and subjected to FACS, separating those cells with only 10% of surface signal left, due to CRISPR targeting (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: The results section explicitly describes this experimental procedure with reference to figures.

claim: DPP4 localizes to the apical brush-border of polarized enterocytes.
source: Dipeptidylpeptidase 4 (DPP4) localizes to the apical brush-border of polarized enterocytes and can be detected with a specific antibody at its extracellular stalk domain.
evidence: Figure 1A caption explicitly states this with accompanying microscopy image.

claim: During polarization, apical DPP4 is increased due to polarized traffic and surface expansion.
source: During polarization, apical DPP4 is increased due to polarized traffic and surface expansion, which can be measured by flow cytometry (right panel, CaCo2 unpolarized versus polarized).
evidence: Figure 1B caption explicitly states this with accompanying flow cytometry data.

claim: HEK293T cells do not express DPP4.
source: HEK293T cells, not expressing DPP4, serve as quality control for staining specificity.
evidence: Figure 1B caption explicitly states this.

claim: Induction of VAC formation with colchicine does not cause a reduction in surface DPP4 signal.
source: Induction of VAC formation with colchicine does not cause a reduction in surface DPP4 signal.
evidence: Figure 1—figure supplement 1B caption explicitly states this.

claim: The percentage of cysts with a single central lumen is substantially decreased in the respective KO cell lines.
source: The percentage of cysts with a single central lumen is substantially decreased in the respective KO cells lines (dot box plot, Mann–Whitney U test. ***p< 0.005, n ≥ 100 cells per condition).
evidence: Figure 4B caption explicitly states this with statistical analysis.

claim: Lamp1-positive compartments appear enlarged upon KO of TM9SF4.
source: The Lamp1-positive compartments appear enlarged upon KO of TM9SF4 (B) and localize to basolateral regions upon KO of ARHGAP33 (C) (white arrowheads).
evidence: Figure 12 caption explicitly states this with reference to microscopy images.

claim: Lamp1-positive compartments localize to basolateral regions upon KO of ARHGAP33.
source: The Lamp1-positive compartments appear enlarged upon KO of TM9SF4 (B) and localize to basolateral regions upon KO of ARHGAP33 (C) (white arrowheads).
evidence: Figure 12 caption explicitly states this with reference to microscopy images.
